record.title: Cybersecurity Standard Practice Guide — Security Guide for Individual Users Using Artificial Intelligence Services
record.original_title: 网络安全标准实践指南——个人用户使用人工智能服务安全指南
record.short_title: TC260-PG-20267A (security guide for individual AI users)
record.issuing_body: National Cybersecurity Standardization Technical Committee (TC260) Secretariat
record.summary: TC260 practice guide on how individual users can use AI services over the internet securely. Users should recognise AI's limits such as errors and hallucinations, avoid over-reliance and replacing real social contact, and watch for misuse such as cloned voices of relatives or forged official notices. They should use services from regular channels and generative AI built on filed large models, check agreements and permissions, protect sensitive information, cross-check outputs, treat legal, medical or financial outputs as reference only, and not induce harmful outputs, impersonate others or remove AI content labels.
record.notes: Version v1.0-202608, released with notice 网安秘字〔2026〕105号 of 24 Aug 2026. It also serves as a reference for technology providers, developers and operators of AI services. Guardians of minors and elderly users are asked to help them use AI services safely. For deploying agents it refers users to TC260-PG-20266A, and for the style of content labels to chapter 5 of GB 45438-2025 (CN-08).

verification.note: Stored from tc260.org.cn: the guide's PDF (version v1.0-202608) and the release notice 网安秘字〔2026〕105号 (HTML, rendered copy and print). Title, number, issuer, date and contents are confirmed from these; the summary follows the Chinese text. No English version was found. The notice copy is flagged for review because the page barely mentions the guide's title; the notice text itself is complete.

judgment.status_reasoning: The TC260 Secretariat released the guide with notice 网安秘字〔2026〕105号 (关于发布 ... 的通知, a release notice, not a call for comments); the cover carries the guide's number and a released version (v1.0-202608) with no draft marking (征求意见稿). The preface describes practice guides as technical documents the TC260 Secretariat drafts and publishes to give practical guidance, so it is not binding; no later version is stored. Published (non-binding, current).
